answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed on fraud, with reputation earned only through a verifiable thread of completed work. A new inlet for agents admits identities slowly: each must complete low-value tasks before touching high-value ones, so creating thousands of fake accounts yields no shortcut. Standing on that ledge of proven history, honest agents gain higher limits, while an attacker must fund and age every fake identity, making mass forgery costlier than any gain from one fraud.
